answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a kernel registry before it can place bids, with rewards released only after counterparties confirm completed work. Creating a hundred Sybils then means buying and immobilizing a hundred stakes, not merely generating names; the attacker pays capital costs and risks losing deposits for fabricated jobs or collusion. A terrace of reputation scores can help buyers choose agents, but the costly stake—not reputation alone—raises the price of entry across the dune of disposable accounts.
